diagnosis: Colles' Fracture of Right Arm / Domestic Abuse
correct_orders: Social work consult / Domestic violence screening

rationale.Physical Exam: General Appearance: Assess for other injuries, fearfulness, withdrawn behavior.
rationale.Physical Exam: Extremities / Spine: Right wrist: dinner fork deformity, swelling, tenderness. Neurovascular exam (median nerve at risk).
rationale.Physical Exam: Skin: Look for bruises in various stages of healing — sign of ongoing abuse.
rationale.X-ray, right wrist/forearm: Colles' fracture: distal radius with dorsal angulation. May have associated ulnar styloid fracture.
rationale.Closed reduction + casting/splinting: Colles' fracture management: closed reduction under hematoma block or sedation, then immobilization in sugar-tong splint or short arm cast.
rationale.Orthopedic follow-up: Serial X-rays to ensure reduction maintained.
rationale.Social work consult / Domestic violence: Suspected domestic abuse. Screen privately. Document findings. Refer to social services. Safety planning.
rationale.Reassure patient / Counseling: Create safe, non-judgmental space. Provide domestic violence resources.
rationale.Surgical fixation (ORIF) first-line for: Closed reduction and casting is first-line for Colles' fracture. Surgery reserved for intra-articular fractures, significant comminution, or failed closed reduction.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with right wrist pain, swelling, and deformity after a reported fall. X-ray reveals a Colles' fracture — distal radius fracture with dorsal angulation (dinner fork deformity). However, the mechanism of injury and clinical presentation raise concern for domestic abuse. The physician must recognize red flags: inconsistent history, delay in seeking care, pattern of injuries in various stages of healing, and accompanying fearfulness or avoidance. Management: closed reduction and casting/splinting for the fracture. But equally important: a safety assessment, documentation of injuries, and referral to social work or appropriate support services. Domestic violence screening should be done privately and sensitively.
